---
title: "Learning path and study plan"
---

This route assumes expert programming skills and teaches the mathematics from
definitions. Chapter numbers retain the site's existing addresses; the order
below follows prerequisites. Time estimates are study suggestions, not promises
of a contest rating. Spend longer wherever you cannot reconstruct a proof.

## Prerequisites, difficulty, and recognition

“Core” describes a mathematical foundation, “advanced” combines foundations,
and “frontier” needs substantial algebraic maturity. A core chapter can still
prepare you for a very hard contest problem.

| Read | Chapter | Prerequisites | Difficulty / recognition |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | [00 Proof](00-foundations/chapter.qmd) | Integer arithmetic | Bridge: quantified claims, invariants, double counts |
| 2 | [01 Modular algebra](01-modular-algebra/chapter.qmd) | 00 | Core–advanced: residue constraints and exponent periods |
| 3 | [02 Number theory](02-multiplicative-number-theory/chapter.qmd) | 00, 01 | Core–advanced: prime powers and gcd filters |
| 4 | [03 Counting](03-combinatorics/chapter.qmd) | 00, 01 units | Core: restrictions, partitions, distinguished elements |
| 5 | [04 Binomials modulo anything](04-modular-binomials/chapter.qmd) | 01, 03 | Core: non-prime moduli and vanishing factorials |
| 6 | [05 Symmetry](05-group-actions/chapter.qmd) | 03, 01 units | Advanced: rotations and relabelling |
| 7 | [06 Polynomials](06-polynomials/chapter.qmd) | 01, 03 | Core–advanced: additive size and batched evaluations |
| 8 | [07 Linear algebra](07-linear-algebra/chapter.qmd) | 01; 06 for fast recurrences | Core–advanced: linear constraints and finite state evolution |
| 9 | [08 Transforms](08-transforms/chapter.qmd) | 00 sets, 01 units, 02 | Advanced: subset/divisor aggregation, bitwise products |
| 10 | [09 Formal series](09-formal-power-series/chapter.qmd) | 06 | Advanced: truncated identities and Newton lifting |
| 11 | [10 Generating functions](10-generating-functions/chapter.qmd) | 03, 06, 09 | Advanced: labelled assembly and coefficient extraction |
| 12 | [11 Set series](11-set-power-series/chapter.qmd) | 03, 08; 09/10 helpful | Advanced: subset convolution and disjoint components |
| 13 | [12 Probability](12-probability/chapter.qmd) | 00; 07 for cyclic systems | Core–advanced: indicators, conditioning, absorption |
| 14 | [13 Discrete sums](13-discrete-sums/chapter.qmd) | 01, 06 | Advanced: huge bounds, floor geometry, rational intervals |
| 15 | [14 Sieves](14-advanced-sieves/chapter.qmd) | 02; 13 for weighted sums | Advanced: repeated quotient states and sparse support |
| 16 | [15 Capstones](15-capstones/chapter.qmd) | Relevant chapters 00–14 | Synthesis: choose and combine models |
| 17 | [16 q-Analogues](16-q-analogues/chapter.qmd) | 04, 07 | Frontier: subspace and rank counting |
| 18 | [17 Field polynomials](17-finite-field-polynomials/chapter.qmd) | 01, 02, 06, 07 | Frontier: Frobenius and factor certification |
| 19 | [18 Graph algebra](18-algebraic-graph-methods/chapter.qmd) | 06, 07, 12 | Frontier: matching and randomized polynomial models |
| 20 | [19 Holonomic](19-holonomic-methods/chapter.qmd) | 06, 07, 09, 10 | Frontier: polynomial-coefficient recurrences |
| 21 | [20 Capstones](20-frontier-capstones/chapter.qmd) | Relevant chapters 16–19 | Synthesis: certification and combined reductions |

Chapter 01's order algorithms accept a factorization as input; Chapter 02
explains its computation. This does not require knowing factorization algorithms
before learning what an order means. Likewise, read probability's elementary
sections early if desired, postponing cyclic linear systems.

## Weekly rhythm

- **Session A (90 min):** derive the chapter's main results by hand.
- **Session B (90 min):** reproduce one key derivation, then solve a problem that
  requires recognizing or adapting it.
- **Sessions C/D (2--3 h each):** one ordered problem per session.  Record when
  each hint was opened.
- **Review (30 min):** re-solve or verbally reconstruct one problem from two or
  six weeks earlier.

Stop a theory session when you can derive the result, state its preconditions,
and explain which statement clues suggest it.  Reading the same proof again is
less valuable than deriving it on a blank page.

## 26-week route

| Weeks | Focus | Gate before moving on |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | [Foundations](00-foundations/chapter.qmd) and [notation](NOTATION.qmd) | Reconstruct induction, Bézout, and a counting or invariant proof. |
| 2--3 | [Modular algebra](01-modular-algebra/chapter.qmd) | Merge non-coprime CRT; explain root/discrete-log existence conditions. |
| 4--5 | [Multiplicative number theory](02-multiplicative-number-theory/chapter.qmd) | Move between prime-power data, Dirichlet convolution, and divisor sums. |
| 6--7 | [Combinatorics](03-combinatorics/chapter.qmd) | Derive IE/binomial-transform identities rather than quote them. |
| 8 | [Binomials modulo anything](04-modular-binomials/chapter.qmd) | Compute a binomial modulo a prime power and a composite without invalid division. |
| 9 | [Group actions](05-group-actions/chapter.qmd) | Build a group action and fixed-object count without naive division. |
| 10--11 | [Polynomials](06-polynomials/chapter.qmd) | Explain every transform contract and solve a problem whose polynomial model is not stated. |
| 12 | [Linear algebra](07-linear-algebra/chapter.qmd) | Define rank/kernel and derive a counting or recurrence model. |
| 13 | [Transforms](08-transforms/chapter.qmd) | Derive transform/inverse pairs from the underlying poset or group. |
| 14--16 | [Formal power series](09-formal-power-series/chapter.qmd) | Derive Newton inverse and exp/log contracts; pass small random tests. |
| 17--19 | [Generating functions](10-generating-functions/chapter.qmd) | Model two unfamiliar classes and derive one Lagrange-inversion answer. |
| 20 | [Set power series](11-set-power-series/chapter.qmd) | Derive ranked subset convolution and explain why exp assembles components. |
| 21 | Revisit [linear algebra](07-linear-algebra/chapter.qmd) applications | Connect polynomial recurrences, determinant counts, and black-box models. |
| 22 | [Probability](12-probability/chapter.qmd) | Write expectation equations with the correct state and conditioning. |
| 23 | [Discrete sums](13-discrete-sums/chapter.qmd) | Derive floor-sum recursion and consecutive-point interpolation. |
| 24 | [Advanced sieves](14-advanced-sieves/chapter.qmd) | Explain quotient blocks and the state/invariant of each sieve family. |
| 25--26 | [Capstones](15-capstones/chapter.qmd) | Complete timed team-style attempts and postmortems. |

Advanced sieves appear late because they are specialized and easier to retain
after divisor inversion and interpolation are mature.  If an imminent contest
is known to favor number theory, move weeks 23--24 directly after week 5.

## A useful problem postmortem

Keep each entry short enough that you will actually reread it:

```text
Problem / date / time before first hint:
Recognition clue I missed:
Mathematical object and decisive identity:
Target complexity and why the naive form failed:
Implementation invariant or bug:
Re-solve dates (+14d, +42d):
```

Mastery means you can recover the solution from the first two lines after six
weeks.  Memorizing an editorial's loop structure does not count.

## Team-contest use

During capstone weeks, use a three-person simulation even when practicing alone:

1. Spend 10 minutes producing only the mathematical model and complexity target.
2. Spend 10 minutes trying to falsify assumptions: prime modulus, invertibility,
   truncation degree, independence, overflow, and forgotten zero cases.
3. Only then implement.  Write down which observations should be communicated
   to a teammate before coding starts.

For a real team, assign one person to derive, one to inspect algebraic contracts,
and one to build a small oracle.  Rotate these roles across problems.

## Weeks 27–33: frontier extension

Begin only after passing the Chapter 15 checkpoint.  These weeks are optional
for regional preparation but valuable for World Finals and strong team contests.

| Weeks | Focus | Gate before moving on |
|---:|---|---|
| 27–28 | [q-Analogues and subspaces](16-q-analogues/chapter.qmd) | Derive the division-free q-binomial recurrence and a rank distribution. |
| 29 | [Finite-field polynomials](17-finite-field-polynomials/chapter.qmd) | Explain all three factorization stages and reconstruct the input from factors. |
| 30–31 | [Algebraic graph methods](18-algebraic-graph-methods/chapter.qmd) | Derive the Tutte cancellation and state a numerical Schwartz–Zippel error bound. |
| 32 | [Holonomic methods](19-holonomic-methods/chapter.qmd) | Convert an ODE to a P-recurrence and certify one guessed recurrence. |
| 33 | [Frontier capstones](20-frontier-capstones/chapter.qmd) | Finish two timed attempts and re-solve one after seven days without topic labels. |

## 24-Chapter Formal Power Series & Generating Functions Study Plan (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`) {#fps-study-plan}

For readers specializing in **Formal Power Series (FPS) and Generating Functions**, or entering after [06 · Polynomials](06-polynomials/chapter.qmd), the 6-Part, 24-Chapter FPS Textbook Track (`Ch 01`–`Ch 24`) provides a self-contained, zero-forward-reference progression from the formal power series ring $K[[x]]$ to Kinoshita–Li $O(N \log^2 N)$ composition, bivariate diagonals, D-finite differential operators, Static Top Tree DP, $q$-series, and Set Power Series.
